citations.description: Ticket snapshot shows comments: [] — no mutation check outputs recorded

findings.criterion: AC8 Mutation check: deleting the confirmation check turns the AC1 and AC3 tests RED; restoring it turns them GREEN. Recorded as a ticket comment with both outputs.
findings.detail: AC8 requires the mutation check results to be recorded as a ticket comment with both RED and GREEN outputs. The ticket snapshot I read shows `"comments": []` — no comments recording this evidence are visible in the ticket snapshot. This criterion requires external evidence (test run outputs) recorded in the ticket, and that evidence is not present in the snapshot I read.
findings.remediation: Run the mutation check (delete the confirmation check at apply_inbound_records.py lines 575-586, run pytest -k 'declines or vendor_collision', record RED output; restore the check, run again, record GREEN output), then post both outputs as a ticket comment.
findings.title: Mutation check evidence not recorded in ticket

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
